about: US answer key rule changes and what each one touches (Brandon t915u, Nov 9 2026 4:40 PM CST; KZ4CP 5:12 PM CST). This file is part of the US rules hash. A rules change rebuilds ONLY the declared states; a park with saved record ids keeps its result through it (kpc_us_key.py) unless the change sets saved_ids: true. One entry per change, newest last: id, when, why, from (the US rules hash it moves FROM: the hash of the last build), scope = {states: ['US-TN', ...], saved_ids: false} or 'all' (every state: only when the change really touches every state). An undeclared change rebuilds the whole key (safe default). Emergency full rebuild by hand: the 'states' input 'all'. Nov 9 evening (KZ4CP 5:41 PM CST): a scope may also list park refs, 'parks': ['US-1234', ...]: only those parks are re-matched (their states are read again, every other park there keeps its result). A scope that lists nothing means ALL; a change that touches no park says scope 'none'.

changes.why: PAD-US load fix (Brandon 11:24 AM CST): saved ids always loaded by id, the state layer before the PAD-US name exception. It changes what every state reads, so every state is rebuilt once; parks with saved ids keep their result.
Bad-ID block list (Brandon t919u; the list is empty) + parks with saved ids keep their result through rule changes (Brandon t915u) + this scope file. Changes no current result.

State GIS paging honors the layer maxRecordCount so a silent server page cap is not treated as the last page, and a short layer already in the saved copy is re-read. It changes what every state may read from a state layer.

A saved copy the master gate holds is refilled first (KPC_REFILL_ONLY: saved PAD-US ids by id and the newer or short state layers, then the same gate again); a re-read that comes back with fewer records than the saved layer no longer replaces it; and every services*.arcgis.com host (services2 to services9 too) is saved-copy only on every path. What a state may read live changes, so every state is rebuilt once.

The master step (before the gate) is now the one writer of the saved copies: the key reads short or new layers into layer files for it (KPC_LAYER_OUT), reads a person's checked download instead of the live layer (KPC_LAYER_IN), and the build only reads the saved copies (KPC_MASTER_OWNS). services-<region>.arcgis.com hosts (services-eu1 and the like) count as services*.arcgis.com, and ncnhde.natureserve.org is never contacted (saved copy only). What a state may read live changes, so every state is rebuilt once.

changes.why: Fresh-start run 42891101784 held FL, UT and DE. The live layer count is now a plain returnCountOnly query: with page and outline parameters, one server counted a single page window (FL DEP state-owned lands 188 of 77,144), one capped the count at the page (NRHP 200), and one refused it (DE state lands). The layer file counts with this state's own entry of a prefix (its where), not the first one. When a short page without exceededTransferLimit leaves records in the state box unread (a server that cuts the row window before the box), the read steps through the layer window by window. What a state reads changes, so every state is rebuilt once.

APPROVED, decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-10

changes.why: Review fixes to the readers. Every layer read is whole or it fails: the read asks the layer's own count and record ids with the same where and box, reads by id, and never keeps a partial layer (the window paging assumed the server's window size and could stop short). PAD-US has the same count check and the same per-layer time limit. One Vermont layer was listed twice and read twice; a layer listed under two prefixes is read once. A park left with no record is graded pin, not official. Host rules come from the one shared guard. Any state layer or PAD-US read could have been cut, so the scope is all.
